artifacts.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

artifacts.synopsis: A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session's will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise.

artifacts.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

artifacts.title: Gendy v. Central Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: A member removed from the rolls under BCO 38-4 challenged Presbytery's ruling that she lacked standing to complain because she was no longer a member. The SJC sustained the complaint: standing under BCO 43-1 cannot be defeated by the very removal challenged. Removal under BCO 38-4 is pastoral discipline, a disciplinary case, not a merely administrative act. The SJC remanded to Presbytery to consider the complaint and take the action it should have taken—remand to the Session. The merits of the removal were not decided.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained a complaint against Philadelphia Presbytery for failing to judge and record TE Larry Smith’s stated difference over the continuation of prophecy and tongues beyond the apostolic era. The record showed Presbytery approved Smith’s transfer exam and defeated a motion to find his view out of accord, but it did not categorize that view in Smith’s own words. The SJC remanded for a written statement and Presbytery’s categorical judgment, without undoing Smith’s transfer or deciding whether his view was erroneous.

artifacts.title: Sawyers et al. v. Missouri Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Elders complained that Missouri Presbytery erred in its BCO 31-2 investigation by finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt that TE Jeffrey Meyers held Federal Vision views contrary to the Westminster Standards. The SJC answered yes: MOP erred under BCO 34-5, and the ordinary remedy was compliance with BCO 31-2. But because MOP had already tried Meyers on April 13–14, 2012, the SJC held further action moot, ordering no additional relief. Adopted by the SJC as a whole, with one dissent.

artifacts.synopsis: Ministers challenged Jeremy Smith's excommunication, but not his deposition. The SJC rejected four allegations and most of the fifth, holding among other things that two ignored citations are only one possible form of contumacy. It sustained the complaint solely because Presbytery wrongly treated Smith's absence as a refusal to appear: a committee email was not a citation by Presbytery. The SJC reversed that finding but did not annul the excommunication, leaving Presbytery to consider whether modification was necessary.

artifacts.synopsis: A minister appealed convictions for contumacy and threatening elders with civil litigation, plus deposition and excommunication. The SJC sustained contumacy as failure to remain subject to the brethren under the ordination vow, not BCO 32-6-type contumacy. It sustained deposition but found excommunication excessive given the conflict and replaced it with indefinite suspension from the sacraments. It did not sustain the threat conviction because the attorney’s letter was absent from the record. A dissent disputed the contumacy ruling.

artifacts.synopsis: After TE Anthony Dallison confessed spousal abuse and received an indefinite suspension, North Florida Presbytery later found him impenitent and deposed him and suspended him from the sacraments. Dallison complained that increasing the censure required fresh charges and trial. The SJC disagreed: his BCO 38-1 confession waived trial rights as to the original charge; the offender then had to satisfy the court of repentance, and the presbytery could investigate and impose higher censure under BCO 37-3, 37-4, 37-8, and 34-4b. The complaint was not sustained.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church appealed its conviction for contumacy and termination of its relationship with Heartland Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, holding that a presbytery lacks original jurisdiction to indict and try a session (lower court) for an offense such as contumacy, as BCO provisions reserve original jurisdiction over ruling elders to the Session level.
